# test_elements_sections_microscopes.py
*`src/pySEA/rayTEM/tests/test_elements_sections_microscopes.py`*

Regression tests for the core Element, MicroscopeSection, and Microscope stack.

These tests use saved `.npy`, `.json`, and `.sea` artifacts as golden outputs.
They validate propagation stability, inferred plane stability, serialization
round trips, and insertion behavior. Several tests create files needed by later
tests, so run order and working directory matter more here than in isolated
unit tests.

---

## Module-level functions

### `test_basic_section_r0()` *(line 17)*
Builds a Drift/Lens/Drift/Lens/Drift section and propagates manually defined
input rays through `fix_ray_dims`. Checks both propagated rays and
`findPlanes(..., axes="x")` against hard-coded/golden results.

### `test_basic_section_wsource()` *(line 41)*
Builds the same style of section with a `Source` element, writes a `.sea` file,
and compares propagated rays against a golden `.npy`.

### `test_every_element()` *(line 56)*
Exercises a mixed section containing `Source`, `Drift`, `Lens`, `Aperture`,
`Quadrapole`, and detector `Drift`. Also calls `section.show(...)` to cover
plot generation.

### `test_dipole_transfer_matrix()` *(line 68)*
Directly checks `Dipole.propagate_ray` for x and y axes using `columnByName` to
assert expected position/angle/z updates.

### `test_basic_microscope_defined_by_lengths()` *(line 86)*
Builds a two-section `Microscope` from element lengths, compares propagated rays
and inferred planes to golden files, then writes JSON and `.sea` microscope
artifacts for reload/insertion tests.

### `test_basic_microscope_defined_by_positions()` *(line 119)*
Builds an equivalent microscope from explicit element/section positions and
compares output against the length-defined golden rays.

### `test_basic_microscope_reload_json()` *(line 137)*
Loads the saved microscope JSON with `load_microscope` and verifies propagation
matches the golden rays.

### `test_basic_microscope_reload_sea()` *(line 151)*
Loads the saved microscope `.sea` file with `load_microscope` and verifies
propagation matches the golden rays.

### `test_element_insertion_microscope()` *(line 175)*
Loads a saved microscope, inserts a zero-strength `Lens` by position, and checks
the final propagated ray plane is unchanged.

### `test_section_insertion_microscope()` *(line 191)*
Builds a microscope, saves a golden propagation, inserts a zero-strength section,
and verifies the final plane remains unchanged. This covers section insertion
without changing optical behavior.
